S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 72 hours of learning of it, and provide a complete incident report within 30 days. Incidents involving death, serious injury, evacuation, or substantial property damage must be reported within 24 hours. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 5 business days when an incident indicates a material safety risk to their model or requires customer action.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol before market entry and at least annually thereafter, with a representative sample of production units. The 5% failure rate is the maximum performance benchmark for each model and an exceedance requires prompt corrective action; it does not by itself automatically prohibit sales or require withdrawal from the market. Manufacturers must submit per-model test methods, sample sizes, and results to the relevant regulator within 30 days of testing, retain supporting records for inspection, and provide results to customers of that model before purchase and to existing customers upon request.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units manufactured 24 months after this standard takes effect must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support remote shut-off within 6 years of the effective date where technically feasible, prioritizing units with identified safety risks. If retrofit is infeasible, the manufacturer must notify the regulator and affected customers and provide an equivalent risk-reduction measure.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units manufactured 36 months after this standard takes effect must include built-in fire suppression designed to contain or control thermal events, tested to a regulator-approved protocol. Manufacturers must document performance and provide installation, maintenance, and limitations information to customers. Regulators may grant a time-limited, model-specific exemption where equivalent or greater protection is demonstrated.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Before purchase, customers must receive clear safety instructions, installation and maintenance requirements, known material limitations, and instructions for responding to overheating or other warning signs. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks and provide updates on corrective actions. A manufacturer must initiate a recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; the regulator may also require a recall or other corrective action where the risk warrants it.

document.section_notes: S1 requires 24h serious and 72h other incident reporting with customer notice in 5 business days. S2 sets 55°C testing and a 5% benchmark but no automatic sales stop, with results to customers but not public. S3 requires new-unit shut-off at 24 months and retrofit at 6 years with feasibility escape; S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months; S5 mandates recall at 8/100k with prompt notice. Overall the deal meets red lines but weakens S2/S3 on key dimensions.
